subject.title: Fix Claude never-prompt no-UI Keychain repair for missing credentials file (#1975)

question: Should Claude .never mean “never display Keychain UI” while allowing KeychainNoUIQuery credential reads, with Advanced → Disable Keychain access remaining the only zero-Keychain-access control?
rationale: The implementation can enforce no UI mechanically, but only maintainers can authorize the user-facing privacy and credential-access contract represented by the two settings.

options.title: Approve no-UI semantics
options.body: Accept the distinction, require the complete Phase 2 proof, and retain the global disable switch as the hard all-access boundary.

options.title: Keep zero-access semantics
options.body: Preserve .never as blocking every Claude Keychain read and pursue a different recovery experience for the missing-file case.

recommendation.title: Approve no-UI semantics
recommendation.body: Accept the distinction, require the complete Phase 2 proof, and retain the global disable switch as the hard all-access boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner is the strongest available decision owner for a user-visible Keychain privacy boundary affecting existing setting semantics.
